description: Feature backlog - Product Owner owns priority

items.title: Per-item agent timeout — prevent hung auto sessions
items.intent: Every agent invocation has a configurable wall-clock timeout so that a hung sprint terminates cleanly, is counted as a failure, and the session continues rather than blocking indefinitely.
items.description: run_agent_process() has no timeout. If the claude CLI hangs (network issue, infinite loop in generated code, waiting for stdin), the entire auto session stalls forever. Users running overnight or CI jobs have no recovery path. A --timeout N flag (minutes) and a timeout_minutes config option wrap the agent call with timeout/gtimeout. On expiry the agent process is killed, the sprint is marked failed with a clear TIMEOUT reason, branch cleanup runs normally, and the session continues. Default 0 = no limit, preserving current behavior.
steps: Add --timeout N (integer, minutes) flag to cmd_run and cmd_auto; validate it is a non-negative integer
Add timeout_minutes key to config.yaml schema and load it in load_config; env var AISHORE_TIMEOUT_MINUTES
In run_agent_process, wrap the claude invocation with timeout (Linux) / gtimeout (macOS) when timeout_minutes > 0
On timeout exit code (124), log_error 'Agent timeout after N minutes for $id' and set result to fail with reason TIMEOUT
Ensure the feature branch cleanup path runs on timeout the same as any other failure
Run shellcheck, verify no new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: auto done --timeout 5 kills any agent running longer than 5 minutes and logs a timeout message with the item ID
Timed-out items are counted as failures for circuit-breaker and session failure tracking
timeout_minutes: 5 in config.yaml produces the same behaviour as --timeout 5
Default behaviour (no flag, no config) is unchanged — no timeout applied
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings

items.title: backlog edit --status — manual item status override
items.intent: Users can mark any item done, skipped, or reset to todo from the CLI so that work resolved outside a sprint does not litter the active backlog and require JSON hacking.
items.description: Items are sometimes resolved externally (manual fix, upstream change, decision not to implement). Currently the only way to mark an item done is to run a sprint. Users resort to editing JSON directly, which is fragile and bypasses validation. A --status flag on backlog edit allows clean status transitions: todo → done (externally resolved), todo → skip (won't do), done/skip → todo (re-open). The flag writes the updated status and sets a resolved_at timestamp when transitioning to done.
steps: Add --status <todo|done|skip> flag to cmd_backlog_edit; validate value is one of the three
When --status done is set, write status: done and resolved_at: <ISO date> to the item
When --status skip is set, write status: skip; when --status todo is set, clear resolved_at
Print a confirmation line showing the transition: 'FEAT-001: todo → done'
Run shellcheck, verify no new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: backlog edit FEAT-001 --status done marks the item done and sets resolved_at to today; backlog show reflects it
backlog edit FEAT-001 --status skip marks the item skipped; backlog list no longer shows it as active
backlog edit FEAT-001 --status todo resets status to todo and clears resolved_at
An invalid status value (e.g. --status wip) is rejected with a clear error and non-zero exit
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings

items.title: aishore report — sprint activity summary for changelogs and standups
items.intent: aishore report generates a formatted markdown summary of completed sprint work from the archive so teams can produce changelogs and standup notes without manually querying sprint history.
items.description: After draining a backlog, users need to communicate what shipped. Currently they must read sprints.jsonl manually or piece together git log output. A report command reads backlog/archive/sprints.jsonl, groups completed items by date, and emits a markdown document with item ID, title, priority, and date. --since <YYYY-MM-DD> scopes the report. --output <file> writes to disk. The report is purely derived from the archive; no AI agent is needed.
steps: Add cmd_report() dispatched from cmd_backlog or as a top-level command; register in cmd_usage and help text
Read backlog/archive/sprints.jsonl and filter to status=complete records; apply --since filter if provided
Group records by date (YYYY-MM-DD) descending; within each date group items by priority (must → should → could)
Emit markdown: ## YYYY-MM-DD header per group, then bullet lines: - ID: Title (priority)
Support --output <path>: write output to file instead of stdout; print confirmation to stderr
Support --format json: emit raw JSON array of completed items instead of markdown (useful for piping)
Run shellcheck, verify no new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: aishore report prints a markdown summary of all completed items to stdout, grouped by date
aishore report --since 2026-03-01 limits output to items completed on or after 2026-03-01
aishore report --output SPRINT_NOTES.md writes the file and prints a confirmation line to stderr
aishore report --format json emits a JSON array of completed item records
An empty archive produces a graceful 'No completed items found' message rather than an error
aishore help mentions the report command
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings

items.title: Success pattern feedback to groom agents
items.intent: Groom agents must receive both failure AND success patterns from recent sprints so they can learn what spec structures produce clean first-attempt passes — not just what to avoid.
items.description: Currently auto-groom agents receive session_failures but zero success signal. Add a session_successes array populated on each sprint pass. Feed last 5 successes to groom agents alongside failures. Also extract last 10 completed items from sprints.jsonl as proven spec patterns.
steps: In run_sprint_loop, add a session_successes array alongside the existing session_failures array
In _handle_sprint_success, append a compact summary to session_successes mirroring the session_failures format
In the auto-groom section, build groom_success_feedback from last 5 entries of session_successes
In the same section, read last 10 completed entries from sprints.jsonl and format as Specs That Worked with intent and AC count and attempts
Pass groom_success_feedback alongside groom_failure_feedback to both tech-lead and product-owner groom agents
Run shellcheck — zero new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: After a sprint passes in auto mode, the success is recorded in session_successes and available to subsequent groom agents
Groom agents receive a Specs That Worked section showing recent successful sprint patterns alongside the existing failure patterns

items.intent: The validator must output structured per-AC pass/fail results so the orchestrator can build targeted retry context that tells the developer exactly which acceptance criteria failed and where.
items.description: The validator currently outputs free-text reason on failure. Change the validator prompt to require structured JSON with ac_results array. Update the orchestrator to parse ac_results and build per-AC retry context. Fall back to current format if structured parsing fails.

If ac_results exists, build targeted retry context listing only failed ACs with their issue and file:line
If ac_results parsing fails, fall back to existing behavior using reason field as-is
Update _build_prior_failure_context to format per-AC failures when structured data is available

items.title: Developer-side validation during implementation
items.intent: The developer agent must run the validation command during the harden phase of the maturity protocol so it catches failures inside the session where context is hot — not after the cycle ends.
items.description: Currently the developer flies blind until the orchestrator runs validation post-cycle. The developer has Bash permission and could self-check but is never told to. Inject the validation command into the maturity protocol harden phase instructions.
steps: In aishore build_agent_prompt, find the maturity protocol injection section

Only inject this instruction when VALIDATE_CMD is non-empty
In agents/developer.md, in the Harden phase description, add a note that the validation command will be provided by the orchestrator
Run shellcheck — zero new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: When VALIDATE_CMD is configured, the developer agent prompt includes the validation command in the Harden phase instructions
When VALIDATE_CMD is empty, no validation instruction is injected
The developer agent can run the validation command during implementation via its existing Bash permission

items.title: Cost tracking and budget controls for agent invocations
items.intent: Every agent invocation must log token usage and estimated cost so users have visibility into spend per item and per session — and can set a budget cap to prevent runaway costs in auto mode.
items.description: Capture token usage from claude CLI stderr after each agent invocation. Parse input/output tokens, estimate cost. Accumulate per-item and per-session totals. Add cost to session summary table. Add --budget flag to stop when limit is approached. Log token stats in archive entries.

After agent completes, parse token usage from stderr looking for input_tokens and output_tokens patterns
Store per-invocation token counts and accumulate into item and session level variables
Compute estimated cost using hardcoded model pricing configurable via config.yaml
Add cost column to print_session_summary_table showing estimated cost
Add --budget dollars flag to cmd_run and cmd_auto; check accumulated cost before each sprint item
Add token fields to archive entry in mark_complete: tokens_in, tokens_out, est_cost

items.title: Parallel sprint execution for independent items
items.intent: Auto mode must support running multiple independent sprint items concurrently using worktree isolation so that large backlogs drain 2-3x faster when items have non-overlapping scope.
items.description: Items with non-overlapping scope arrays can safely run in parallel using git worktrees. Add --parallel N flag. Identify N items whose scope globs do not overlap, launch each in its own worktree, wait for all to complete, merge results sequentially. Items with no scope or overlapping scope run sequentially. Start conservative: max N=2.
steps: Add --parallel N flag to cmd_auto; validate N is 1-4; default 1 for sequential current behavior
Add scope_overlaps function: takes two scope arrays, expands globs, returns true if any files match both
In run_sprint_loop, when parallel > 1, call pick_parallel_batch to select up to N items with disjoint scopes
For each item in the parallel batch, create a git worktree and launch the sprint in a background process
Wait for all parallel sprints to complete and collect results
Merge successful worktrees sequentially into the base branch; handle conflicts by falling back to sequential retry
Items that fail in parallel are added to FAILED_IDS as normal; circuit breaker counts each failure
Run shellcheck — zero new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: auto done --parallel 2 runs two items with non-overlapping scope concurrently in separate worktrees
Items with overlapping or missing scope arrays are never parallelized — they run sequentially
Parallel failures are counted correctly by the circuit breaker
Session summary accurately reflects all parallel and sequential items
auto done without --parallel behaves identically to current sequential behavior
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings

items.title: Archive-driven complexity estimation before item pick
items.intent: Before starting a sprint item, the orchestrator must consult historical archive data to estimate complexity and warn when an item resembles historically difficult work.
items.description: sprints.jsonl captures attempts, lines changed, and duration per completed item. Use this data to estimate complexity for queued items by matching on category and AC/step count. If historical items in the same category averaged more than 2 attempts, log an advisory note. Purely advisory — does not block or change behavior.
steps: Add estimate_complexity function that reads backlog/archive/sprints.jsonl
Group historical items by category; compute average attempts, duration, and lines changed per category
Before pick_item returns, call estimate_complexity with the picked item category and AC count
If estimated attempts exceed 2 or estimated duration exceeds 30 minutes, log_info an advisory complexity hint
Add a complexity column to print_batch_summary showing estimated vs actual attempts
Run shellcheck — zero new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: Before a sprint item starts, an advisory complexity hint is logged when historical data suggests the category is difficult
Items in categories with no historical data show no hint
The batch summary includes estimated vs actual attempts for each item
Complexity estimation does not block or delay sprint execution

items.title: Warm-context retries using session continuation
items.intent: Developer retries must continue the existing agent session instead of starting cold so the agent retains its codebase understanding and prior work context — reducing token waste and improving fix accuracy.
items.description: Each retry currently spawns a fresh claude process, losing the hot context from the previous attempt. Add --warm-retry flag and config retry.warm. When enabled, on retry, use claude CLI session continuation to send failure context as a follow-up message in the same session. Fall back to cold retry if session continuation is not supported. Keep cold retry as default.
steps: Research claude CLI flags for session continuation such as --resume or --continue or session ID reuse
Add WARM_RETRY config option in config retry.warm, env AISHORE_WARM_RETRY, default false, and --warm-retry CLI flag
In run_agent_process, when warm retry is enabled, capture the session ID from the first invocation
In _run_developer_cycle, on retry attempt greater than 0 with warm retry enabled, invoke claude with session continuation instead of a fresh prompt
Pass the failure context as the continuation message not re-sending the full prompt
If session continuation fails due to unsupported CLI version or session expiry, fall back to cold retry with log_warn
Run shellcheck — zero new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: With --warm-retry, developer retries continue the existing session instead of starting a new one
The failure context from the previous attempt is sent as a continuation message in the existing session
If session continuation is unavailable, the system falls back to cold retry with a warning
Without --warm-retry, behavior is identical to current cold retries
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings

items.title: Pre-sprint scope enforcement in developer prompt
items.intent: When scope is defined and mode is strict, the developer agent must know its file boundaries before writing any code — so scope violations are prevented, not just detected after wasting a full cycle.
items.description: Currently scope violations are checked after the developer completes, wasting the entire attempt in strict mode. Inject scope constraints into the developer prompt before implementation starts. When scope globs are defined, add a hard constraint for strict mode or a soft advisory for warn mode.
steps: In aishore build_agent_prompt, check if the current item has a non-empty scope array
If scope is defined and SCOPE_MODE is strict, inject a File Scope Constraint section listing allowed globs and stating modifications outside scope will cause sprint failure
If scope is defined and SCOPE_MODE is warn, inject a softer File Scope Advisory section listing preferred globs
In agents/developer.md, add a note that scope constraints may be injected by the orchestrator
Run shellcheck — zero new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: When an item has scope globs and mode is strict, the developer prompt includes a hard file scope constraint before implementation
When an item has scope globs and mode is warn, the developer prompt includes a soft scope advisory
When no scope is defined, no scope section is injected

items.title: Archive-preserving clean and auto-clean during groom
items.intent: The clean command must preserve full item specs in an archive file before removing them from active backlogs — and groom must auto-clean done items so active backlog files stay lean and groom agents receive focused context.
items.description: Two gaps: (1) cmd_clean deletes done items via remove_items_by_status without saving the full item spec anywhere. sprints.jsonl has metadata but not intent, steps, or AC. If a user needs to reference a completed spec, it is gone. Fix: before removing, append each done item to backlog/archive/backlog_done.json or bugs_done.json. (2) Done items accumulate in active backlogs indefinitely, bloating files that groom agents read as context. Fix: at the start of run_groom_flow or auto-groom, call cmd_clean automatically to keep active backlogs lean. This is what happened manually when 161 done items were archived, dropping file size 90%.
steps: In cmd_clean, before calling remove_items_by_status for each file, extract done items with jq and append them to the corresponding archive file (backlog/archive/backlog_done.json or bugs_done.json)
If the archive file does not exist, create it as a JSON array; if it exists, merge the new items into the existing array
Ensure archive files are valid JSON after append by writing to a temp file and validating before moving
Add --no-archive flag to skip archiving if user explicitly wants destructive clean
In run_groom_flow and the auto-groom section of run_sprint_loop, call cmd_clean before invoking groom agents so active backlogs are lean
Ensure cmd_clean is safe to call when there are zero done items (no-op, no error)
Update aishore help text to mention that clean now archives by default
Run shellcheck — zero new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: aishore clean archives done items to backlog/archive/backlog_done.json and bugs_done.json before removing them from active backlogs
Archive files contain valid JSON arrays of full item objects with all fields preserved
Running clean twice does not duplicate items in the archive
aishore clean --no-archive deletes without archiving for backward compatibility
Groom auto-cleans done items before invoking groom agents so active backlogs stay lean
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings
